Mia Chen: Heads-up — after the runtime deploy at 04:30 UTC EU region prefix/KV cache hit-rate collapsed to ~38% (was ~80-85%). p50/p95 token latency up ~2x. Anyone else seeing this?
Raj Patel: confirming metrics ingestion. us-west still at ~82%. Looks region-specific. No infra alerts.
Linh Nguyen: interesting — did we change kernel/serialization in the FP16 kernel swap? I recall a change to how prefix keys are serialized before hashing.
Sam Ortiz: checking commits — the kernel-select change (commit 12f3a9c) included a micro-optim that reordered tensor meta -> could alter stable key bytes.
Mia Chen: logs show many "kv_lookup miss; falling back to compute" across EU. Example: 
```
[2026-03-16T04:35:12Z] region=eu-west req_id=0x... prefix_hash=0x8a3 miss
[2026-03-16T04:35:12Z] fallback_compute_ms=37
```
Seems like the same prefixes that are hot in us-west are cold in eu-west.
Raj Patel: profiling IPC + cache lookup: KV cache CPU share increased from 4% -> 12% but hit-rate drop caused more fallback compute, overall CPU up. Trace shows serialization time unchanged, but hash buckets show skew.
Linh Nguyen: two hypotheses: 1) keying/serialization change made keys incompatible across kernels (so replicated keys hashed differently), or 2) routing policy change increased cross-region distribution of unique prefixes (cache fragmentation).
Sam Ortiz: routing policy was adjusted yesterday: weights for global routing set to use local preference then random fallback. That increases cross-region spread when local capacity low. Might increase cold populations.
Mia Chen: can we confirm if prefix keys are identical bytes across regions for the same request? Would catch serialization mismatch.
Raj Patel: grabbed a sample of serialized prefix bytes from reproducer across us-west + eu-west. They differ — ordering field "seq_len" moved before token ids after the kernel change. So serialization changed.
Linh Nguyen: that explains it. Replication uses key bytes to sync cache; if serialization differs between runtime builds in regions, replicated keys don't match -> misses.
Mia Chen: immediate mitigation options: 
- roll back kernel-select change in EU to restore previous serialization (fast)
- implement versioned cache key (major/minor) so keys are stable across formats (safe long-term)
- pre-warm EU with hot prefixes from us-west via async replication that normalizes keys (stop-gap)
Sam Ortiz: rollback is easiest for now. We should also add CI to detect serialization changes in the build matrix.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0472 — EU prefix cache regression. Assigned to @Mia Chen, priority P2.
deploy-bot: Deploy job #bb-1123 rolled back on eu-west cluster at 05:10 UTC (success).
Raj Patel: after rollback hit-rate back to ~81% and latency normalized. Leaving the thread open to discuss long-term fixes.
Linh Nguyen: long-term: add a key-version header and normalize on replication, plus a lightweight compatibility shim in KV read path to accept old/new ordering for a probation period. Also a test that serializes canonical prefixes across all supported kernel builds.
Sam Ortiz: also worth examining routing: if routing spreads unique prefixes thinly, even with serialization stable we'll have lower hit-rate. Suggest tuning routing policy to favor sticky routes for high-volume clients or enable region-local replication of hot keys.
Mia Chen: agreed. Action items: 
- Raj: add key-versioning PR + unit tests (ETA 2d)
- Linh: add serialization snapshot check to CI (ETA 3d)
- Sam: run routing sim to estimate hit-rate impact by strategy and propose change (ETA 4d)
- Ops: keep pre-warm playbook ready for new regions
Raj Patel: note from profile after rollback: KV lookup CPU % dropped, fallback compute dropped 60% during peak. I'll attach traces to the incident.
Mia Chen: thanks all. New follow-ups: add a small doc in eng-runtime describing cache key invariants and upgrade rules so we avoid accidental incompatible kernel swaps in prod.
Sam Ortiz: tl;dr — serialization change caused multi-region coherence break; rollback fixed it; plan: key-versioning, CI checks, routing simulation, pre-warm playbook.
Linh Nguyen: also flag for release engineering — coordinate kernel ABI/serialization changes across regions in the release notes.
Mia Chen: closing thread once PRs are opened. :thumbsup:
